answer: A sybil tax makes bulk forgery unprofitable. Each new identity pays a sunk fee of 200 credits before trading, like a walnut vendor paying a stall fee that is never refunded. An agent that wants to wander to a new marketplace pays again at each gate, so 100 fake identities cost 100 x 200 = 20,000 credits, lost even if the fakes are banned. No fable trick recovers a sunk fee. An honest agent pays once and earns undiluted rewards.
